Name: CA. Suyog Upadhyaya
Question: Is CA really tough?
Answer: I qualified CA after failing 2 years straight! Let me tell you my story! I come from a very good academic background, from ranking 3rd in my District in 10th grade SLC 11 years back, to almost scoring a rank in CA-Intermediate level back in 2013, I’ve been quite a studious student. Everything was going smooth, not like a cake walk but not a path of thorns either. But then, CA-Final Happened! I joined a CA- Internship which would not allow me to join any classes (back then online classes were not as popular as they are now) and whenever, I joined any class, I’d get out-stationed which would make me miss around 75% of the total class. Normal working hours would be around 16–17 during peak time (4–5 months straight). There are instances where I’d leave home at 6AM, attend my lectures, report to office at 10:30 and then back to home at around 2AM. And with all the unhealthy food from “starred” hotels, and no exercise plus some other unhealthy habits and choices, I got serious health problems, both physical and mental. I was burnt out. (Class in New Delhi: Circa. Feb 2017) I skipped my November,2016 & May 2017 examinations (ICAI conducts exams semi-annually in May and November) as I was quite unprepared and had a baggage of obesity, fatty liver, depression, High cholesterol level, fatigue, palpitation, severe back pain to name a few. (Nepal, Circa. June 2017) I moved to Varanasi, and had a realization that I had enough of these issues. I started taking care of my body. I followed a workout regimen and started studying Indian scriptures mostly Ayurveda and Philosophy along with studying CA Books. (Varanasi: Our Nepali Mandir on top, it has very good vibrations if you want to meditate and bottom two are pictures of our Dharmashaalaa) Then came November, 2017 attempt. I was prepared for my exams, but for some strange reason, in my first paper of Financial Reporting, I reached my Center 30 minutes late (because of unexpected traffic and a goof up) and afterwards, I got blank for 20 minutes. Later, I realized, it was due to antibiotics, which I consumed a month before for my skin problems. I managed to pass all the papers except that one and because of that, I had to take Group-I again (There are 2 groups of papers, 4 each.) Failed because of ICAI’s System Okay, come May, 2018 paper. This time I was sure I’d pass. And, here I failed again because of “Auditing” paper. The irony, I worked at an Audit firm for 3 years. I asked for revaluation and found out that the examiner, for some strange reasons, decided to give 1 out of 4 marks for every question attempted, even if my answers were 100% matching with ICAI’s suggested answers. Because of ICAI’s strange rules, we cannot challenge the examiner. I was very sad and was very angry as well, but this time, I was working out, had my diet in check and had reversed almost all my health problems. I was into meditation and acquired a lot of knowledge in Indian Ayurvedic Systems, Philosophy and spirituality. There were a lot of doubts and a lot was happening in family as well, but that was totally understandable. I was hurt, for sure, but I was pretty confident. I decided to take this one last attempt and finally passed in November, 2018. So, Is CA Really Tough? No. It just requires a lot of discipline not only in studies but also in life overall. Take care of your physical , mental and spiritual health. Follow a workout regimen. If you’re interested I’ve made a beginner workout program: FREE 30 Day Home Workout For Beginners To Lose Weight Or if you’re interested in Yoga: Get Your 30 Days Beginner's Yoga Program Make sure to meditate and keep the positivity and the discipline in track. You can check out my bio to connect with (If you use Pinterest or Instagram), if you’d like help in your journey. What about revaluations? Yes, that is a sad part, and we are working a lot. We even protested back in September, 2019 against it. I, along with other teachers will make sure there is an amendment so that no one would have to go through the pain, that I , and thousands of other students went through. (September, 2019: Protest against ICAI as a Member) How is your journey going by? Let me know in the comments below. Wishing you good health and a good life.

Therefore, kidney patients should be cautious while doing Prolonged Fasting. Question: What are the 7 best exercise tips?
Answer: I have been exercising for past 3 years, and there are many tips that I’d like to pass on from my experience. Here’s the best 7 ones: 1.Follow a workout program: Failing to plan is planning to fail. Always follow a particular workout program, designed in such a way that your muscles get taxed in a progressive way. You don’t want to under/over train. And, a workout program will keep you motivated to do complete the predefined tasks and measure your progress as well. Can check out the Free 30 day workout program here: FREE 30 Day Home Workout For Beginners To Lose Weight Or, if you’re into bodyweight and yoga, you can get the free 30 day yoga here: Get Your 30 Days Beginner's Yoga Program 2. Pre workout warm up: Do some dynamic mobility warm-ups before working out. Avoid stretching, just do some mobility training. It warms up your muscles, and reduces the rate of injury. Even Bruce Lee didn’t do warmup before his routine and got a back injury. From the Archives : Bruce Lee's Back Injury You can follow this 5 minute routine: 3. Post workout Stretches: Post workout stretches is very important especially if you’re lifting heavy. It makes easier for the muscles to deal with the injuries. It saves you a lot of injury trouble and with DOMS as well. You can simply follow this 5 minutes stretch. 4. Do not miss out on cardio: Strength and all is okay but if you can’t run, there’s not point in your fitness. Remember to do strength training before cardio. 5. For busy schedule : If you’re short on time, then High Intensity Interval Training is a go to option. Too much work in too less time. It requires you to give your full efforts for a short period of time and then rest for a certain time and again , giving your full efforts. Example: Run as hard as you can for 20 seconds, then for 30 seconds, do simple jogging, then again run hard for 20 seconds and jog for 30 seconds. (You can reduce jog time, as per you fitness level). Do this for about 15–20 minutes. 6. Don’t miss out on breathing exercises/pranayama: I can’t emphasize enough the role of breathing exercises in your workout regimen. It helps in quick recovery, improves your strength, endurance and immunity. One very little example: I could only do 5–6 pull-ups, but after I incorporated pranyama, I could easily do 10 pull-ups. It will defer from person to person. What you can do is: Take 30 deep breaths (During inhalation, your belly and chest should expand and should squeeze during exhalation), and then on the last breath hold it. Hold it as much as you can, typically 1–2 minutes, it depends on your fitness level. Continue it for 2–3 rounds. You can include other pranyama like Kapalbhaati or Anulom Vilom 7. Nutrition/Water and Intermittent Fasting: Have plenty of fresh raw fruits and vegetables. Take ample amount of Fats like ghee, butter, nuts etc. Drink water by checking how your body responds. There is no specific number of liters of water per day one should drink. Make sure the pee is clear and you don’t feel dehydrated. Intermittent fasting is a must for exercise doers, as during the workout, old muscles get damaged and new muscle originates. The dead muscle proteins are not excreted which creates problem in our body like ageing, arthritis etc. During intermittent fasting, the dead proteins get excreted and will help tremendously on your overall health. Question: How do you stop beating yourself up when you made the big mistake of your life?
Answer: First of all, I’d like the seeker to know that they are on the right track if they are beating themselves up after making the big mistake of their life. Because, it means that they have realized their mistake which most people fail to do and end up in vicious cycles hurting others. The world runs on cause and effect. The mistake is the cause, the guilt is the effect. Yes, there are various external effects as well, but the most foundational ones are the sensations within. The effect comes up to give us learning, to break the cycle of karma (Cause/Work) and its “Fala” (Effect/Result). When we understand the the beating up that we are experiencing is the basic natural phenomenon then , we realize that we have to take it as an opportunity to learn and evolve. I’m no way an expert , because there are times where I make mistakes and I repent. Not always I am in a great unison with my senses. But here is a simple technique I use: Firstly, take 10–15 deep breaths, and then observe normal breath for about 5 minutes. Then observe the sensations from top of the head to tips of the toes. During the time many thoughts will come, do not try to avoid it, rather focus on sensations. Then recreate the whole scenario and try analyzing the situation from first person view (i.e., your own view). Analyse why you did what you did. What made you do such? What were the circumstances then, explore possible explanations. There will be many. Then, observe the scenario from second person perspective (For example if you had an argument, try watching the scenario from the view of person with whom you argued). Feel how the second person would have felt and why the did what they did. Finally, observe the scenario from a neutral perspective. Like you’re watching a movie but detached with the character. Analyse why it happened. Yes, it will not go in a single instance, there is no magic pill. Rather its like a workout. Take your time to realize that what had been done/said cannot be undone, and the best thing we can do is to mend the situation by making rational decisions formed after continuous exercise as mentioned above. You’ll certainly evolve as a better human being than you were before. Do not shy away from asking for forgiveness or giving forgiveness. Our human life is very short. I wish you a happy life. Regards, S

Question: What is the deal with the present trend of "intermittent" fasting for weight loss?
Answer: Intermittent Fasting has been the style of eating since the beginning of history (Picture Source: Pixabay) Early humans, used to hunt food and then go off food for days. Our body has been evolved in a similar fashion. If you observe wild animals, they will hunt , savor the meat, and then go days without food. Intermittent fasting has been the way of life for the animals. (Picture source: Pixabay) According to Ayurveda (Indian traditional medicine system) , it is suggested to eat dinner well before sunset and then again breaking the fast a few hours after the sunrise, the next morning. This will take about 14–16 hours, and can be considered as Intermittent Fasting. Many religions like Hindus, Muslims etc have been observing fasting in various occasions since thousands of years. So, telling it a “present trend” will be wrong. So why Intermittent Fasting? (Picture source: Wall Street Journal) The main benefit of Intermittent Fasting is Autophagy. As you can see, Yoshinori Oshumi, a Japanese researcher, has been awarded Nobel Prize for his discoveries of mechanisms for autophagy induced by Fasting. I’m trying to explain it in a rather simple way. Our cells keeps on dying and regenerating but not necessarily we are able to excrete the dead cells. The cells are stored in our body. When we are always in a feeding mode, we are not able to digest and excrete the dead cells because our body is busy in breaking down the food that we have ingested (not necessarily absorbed). In a fasted state, there’s nothing to digest hence, the body digests off the dead cells. It is way too vague to explain this way but the basic is the same only. (Picture Source: Pixabay) Now, you go to the gym, you have flaccid body then you do workouts, your body becomes sore and then you’ll have defined and toned muscles. How do the toned muscles form? It is formed by breaking of “unworked” muscle fibres and constant regeneration process. Now where do the old muscles go? They are stored in our body only! And constant accumulation of it results your body becoming a garbage can. The best way to throw it away , you got it right - “Autophagy”. And the best part, Intermittent Fasting actually helps in building those muscles!! There are numerous other benefits of Intermittent Fasting , like increased Metabolism, increment in Growth Hormone secretion, better handling of stress, reduction in Kidney diseases, increased longevity so on and so forth. There are multiple researches done to back this claim. And weight loss, or I should say “Fat Loss” is just a “Side-effect”

Take Action : After Introspection, we need to take action, mostly on the missing links. Most of the time, after introspection, we take action because we come closer to the reality as it is. And then again Re-introspect. It is a continuous cycle. These are abstract concept and subjective to individuals. So, what has worked for me? 1.Physical Fitness and Health: I was unhealthy and obese in my late teen and early twenty. I realized I had to take my physical fitness in line before I’d be hospitalized and god knows what. I gradually started with beginner’s workouts. I couldn’t even do 3 push-ups in a row. Following a workout plan always helps. You can check out Beginner’s Workout program here : 30 Day Beginner’s Workout Program . That’s what I used, in case you are wondering. I lost around 30 Kilograms (about 66 pounds) in total, over the span of 1.5 years. With healthy eating, my face had a different glow and improved my overall personality. 2. Rigorous Learning & Study : Learn continuously , about various topics. Our life is multidimensional. Although I am a Chartered Accountant, I continuously study about Technology , Astrology, Astronomy, Psychology, Philosophy, and many other topics. I am just open to knowledge and I have realized that I do not know anything. Trying to get perspective will certainly help in developing personality. Knowledge is free over the internet, you’re just a search away from it. 3. Being True to Self: Many a times, we try to portray ourselves as someone whom we are not. Vipassanā meditation has helped me being true to myself, and to the people around me. This has helped me throw away the wrong beliefs that I have of me, although not easily but gradually. I am still learning this process and I’m very grateful for having this opportunity. 4. Gratitude (As much as possible) : It is the most important skill to build, because nobody wants to get treated badly. Although apparently it feels like being grateful leads to us getting misused, however, If we become more grateful, good things come our way. I have learned this hard way (Still learning, doesn’t come naturally to me ). Don’t try to become a jerk because: (Pic credit: Kingsman Twitter Account) “This aint that kind of movie, Bruv!” What do you do, to improve your personality? Let me know in the comments, we can definitely learn from each other.
